subject.title: [Feature]: Store configuration backup files in their own directory, with datetime name convention

question: Should OpenClaw make this issue the canonical direction for a dedicated `config-backup/` directory with datetime names, or should core keep adjacent backups and limit any change to naming/docs?
rationale: The implementation is feasible, but backup layout affects config recovery, sensitive backup permissions, legacy `.bak.N` retention, doctor docs, and overlapping timestamp-only work, so automation should not choose the permanent product contract alone.

options.title: Adopt Dedicated Directory Layout
options.body: Use this issue as the canonical design and require a migration-safe implementation covering legacy adjacent backups, recovery, permissions, retention, audit text, doctor docs, and tests.

options.title: Limit Scope To Timestamp Suffixes
options.body: Keep backups adjacent and route naming-only work through https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/39923 and its linked PR, then separately narrow or close this directory request.

options.title: Keep Current Backup Ring
options.body: Reject the layout change for now and document the adjacent numbered backup ring as the intended stable behavior.

recommendation.title: Adopt Dedicated Directory Layout
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the canonical design and require a migration-safe implementation covering legacy adjacent backups, recovery, permissions, retention, audit text, doctor docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history and discussion context across the config backup, recovery, and test surfaces.
